newsitem.title: UK: Fiba Nordic welcomes probe into DMG funds.
newsitem.headline: Fiba Nordic welcomes probe into DMG funds.

text.p: Fiba Nordic Securities (FNS), the London-based broker now involved in the storm over holdings of three temporarily-suspended Morgan Grenfell European funds, said on Thursday it welcomed investigation from any regulator.

"I'm sure the Securites and Futures Authority (SFA) is investgating and FNS will cooperate with them and any other regulator. It is very important that the investigation goes ahead and everybody finds out all the information," a spokesman for FNS said.
The Serious Fraud Office announced on Thursday it had become involved in the probe after information was passed to it by the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO).
The funds were suspended on Monday pending an investigation by IMRO into holdings of unquoted and prelisted stocks in the funds. Trading in all three funds resumed on Thursday.

FNS sold unlisted securites to, and valued securites for the three funds managed by Peter Young and Stewart Armer, who have both now been suspended by Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, part of the Deutsche Bank Group.
Press reports and fund management sources have suggested that the relationship between FNS and Young was unusually close.

But the spokesman said FNS had a normal professional relationship with Peter Young, the manager of two of the funds. "It is a pefectly straightforward business relationship although obviously with a big, important client."
"Peter Young and (FNS director) Eric Langaker have a purely business relationship and anything you hear to the contrary is untrue. They have ever only been on one visit together."

The spokesman confirmed that FNS is a UK-based company owned by "a couple of private Luxembourg investment companies." Fiba Nordic in Norway, which owns 10 percent of the London Fiba Nordic Securities was set up at the same time "and there is an associate company in Sweden", he added. Asked what proportion of FNS business was with Morgan Grenfell, the spokesman said it depended how it was added up.
"It certainly wasn't their single biggest client but depending on when you draw the line it was around 10 percent, probably. It was not out of the ordinary."
He said FNS came up with valuations of unquoted and prelisted stocks at Morgan Grenfell's request. "It had a method by which to value these businesses which MG was well aware of."

There was also nothing unusual in what stock FNS was offering and what Young bought for the funds. "Morgan Grenfell and Peter Young were a client, and they acted like a broker, buying and selling shares and introducing them."
"It is wrong to suggest it was different from anything any other broker would do for an institutional client."

FNS could not divulge what stocks it had offered and what had been bought by Young for the three funds, which have a total of some 1.4 billion stg under management. Asked about FNS' involvement with Russ Oil & Technology, the Luxembourg company named on Wednesday alongside Young in a UK High Court writ to freeze their assets, the FNS spokesman confirmed FNS had helped to set up Russ Oil, but did not own it.
"Yes they were involved in the normal way in setting up the Russ Oil company, as they have been in others, under the instruction of their client," he said.

The five point writ seeks to restrain Young and Russ Oil & Technology from dealing in warrants or shares issued by Xavier Mines. The warrants gave Young and the Luxembourg company the right to buy 15.5 million shares in Xavier Mines at a fixed price of 9.15 Swedish crowns a share.
